clue.lookalike-domain: The sender domain imitates ours (zero for o, extra word or letter).
clue.urgency: Artificial urgency pushes you to act before thinking.
clue.link-mismatch: The real link address does not match what the text shows.
clue.external-sender: The sender is outside the company and unexpected.
clue.unexpected-attachment: An attachment nobody asked for, often a zip or macro file.
clue.generic-greeting: A generic greeting: the sender does not know your name.
clue.authority-pressure: It claims to be a boss and demands something unusual.
clue.secrecy: It asks you to keep quiet and skip the usual checks.
clue.asks-credentials: Real IT never asks for your password or MFA code.
clue.internal-sender: The sender is a real internal address.
clue.real-link: The link points to the real intranet domain.
clue.expected-context: It matches routine work and asks for nothing risky.
clue.normal-baseline: It matches the normal baseline for this user or job.
clue.user-confirmed: The user confirmed the change themselves.
clue.many-failures: Many failed logins in a row point to password guessing.
clue.external-ip: The address is outside the company network.
clue.success-after-failures: A success after many failures means the guess may have worked.
clue.impossible-travel: Two logins too far apart in too little time: someone else is using the account.
clue.sqli-pattern: The quote and -- are classic SQL injection.
clue.data-exfil: A huge upload to an unknown address looks like data theft.
clue.off-hours: It happened at an hour when nobody should be working.
day.soc-day-1.title: First shift
day.soc-day-1.brief: Welcome to the Halcyon SOC. Learn the queue: mark each item legit, phishing or escalate.
day.soc-day-1.debrief: Most phishing shows itself in the sender and the link. Check both before anything else.
day.soc-day-2.title: After the test
day.soc-day-2.brief: The security test showed weak spots. Now the queue has login alerts and logs too.
day.soc-day-2.debrief: A single log line rarely tells the story. Compare it with the normal baseline.
day.soc-day-3.title: Busy Monday
day.soc-day-3.brief: More mail, trickier senders. Some lookalike domains differ by a single character.
day.soc-day-3.debrief: Attackers register domains one character away from yours. Read them letter by letter.
day.soc-day-4.title: The kit in action
day.soc-day-4.brief: You saw the phishing kit from the inside. Now catch its emails in the queue.
day.soc-day-4.debrief: Knowing how a kit works makes its mails easy to spot: urgency plus a lookalike link.
day.soc-day-5.title: Long queue
day.soc-day-5.brief: Ten items. Do not let alert fatigue make you skip the clues.
day.soc-day-5.debrief: Fatigue is an attack surface. Good tooling shows the clues for you.
day.soc-day-6.title: The pretext
day.soc-day-6.brief: Attackers pretend to be bosses and IT. Authority is their favourite lever.
day.soc-day-6.debrief: Pressure plus secrecy is the signature of social engineering. Verify through another channel.
day.soc-day-7.title: Credentials
day.soc-day-7.brief: Attackers now ask for credentials and MFA codes in believable ways.
day.soc-day-7.debrief: No legitimate team asks for your password or MFA code. Ever.
day.soc-day-8.title: The quiet intrusion
day.soc-day-8.brief: Fewer emails, more logs. Someone may already be inside.
day.soc-day-8.debrief: Intruders blend in. Odd hours and odd volumes are how you find them.
day.soc-day-9.title: Mixed storm
day.soc-day-9.brief: Everything at once. Prioritise: escalate what could mean data loss first.
day.soc-day-9.debrief: Triage means ordering by impact. A data leak outranks a suspicious email.
day.soc-day-10.title: The attacker returns
day.soc-day-10.brief: The attacker from the incident is back. Handle the queue and protect Halcyon.
day.soc-day-10.debrief: You now read mail, logins and logs like an analyst. Next: defend the network itself.
